34.title: The Universe Power System
34.003.p: Primordial force originates in the space potentials of the Unqualified Absolute and represents the unrevealed energies which do not initially respond to direct Paradise gravity, and the mere passive presence of the Primary Master Force Organizers is enough to convert this space potential into primitive force activity[42:2.10], while these organizers direct this force toward its first modification state as primary emergent energy under the supervisory domain of the Unqualified Absolute[29:5.5].
34.005.p: Primary emergent energy, or segregata, is the organized, directional, mass-emphasizing, tension-bearing energy system derived from primordial force and still does not initially and certainly respond to Paradise gravity while reflecting collective mass response and directional tendencies of space[42:2.11].
34.007.p: Gravity-energy is the stage at which energy begins to definitely react to absolute Paradise gravity and exhibits the potential for linear gravity response inherent in emergent mass and electronic formation, becoming the active ancestor of all universe matter and enabling the domain of the Universe Power Directors once gravity response fully appears[42:2.12]. The combined designation for segregata and gravita is “Ultimata” on Uversa [42:2.13].
34.010.p: The Seven Supreme Power Directors, personal offspring of the Seven Master Spirits acting corporately, are quasi-material beings eternally associated one-to-one with each Master Spirit, stationed around Paradise and phenomenally indicating the directional presence of power focus for each superuniverse, functioning singly in superuniverse power-energy regulation and corporately in central creation administration [29:1.2]~3.
34.012.p: The Supreme Power Centers are long-existent living beings who distribute energy efficiently to sub-constellations and systems, provide concentrated power-lines utilized for interplanetary communication and transport, and establish direct energy circuits between centers and controllers throughout the grand universe [29:2.17].
34.014.p: The Master Physical Controllers, physical descendants of the Power Centers and scattered throughout the seven superuniverses, execute physical adjustments, circuit establishment, electronic control and ultimatonic manipulation under the directive presence of the Power Directors, being uniform in structure except for minor tonal variations in each superuniverse [29:1.4].
34.016.p: Morontia Power Supervisors constitute the fourth group of the Universe Power Directorate and operate on the morontia transition levels, effecting organization and regulation of energy on planes where physical and spiritual realities coexist, holding responsibility for morontia circuits and stabilizing energies designed for transition forms and ascendant life[29:0.9].
34.019.p: Primary Master Force Organizers reside on Paradise but operate throughout the unorganized and pre-material space regions of the master universe, acting under the Architects of the Master Universe and initiating nebular vortices, stimulating vast energy cyclones and transforming primordial force into segregata, prior to its response to Paradise gravity[29:5.1][29:5.5].
34.021.p: Associate Transcendental Force Organizers receive the segregata processed by the primary organizers and further advance it into gravita, and once a Creator Son arrives to complete universe plans, they yield to the power directors, functioning thereafter in accordance with superuniverse authority to refine energies for actualized material structure [29:5.6].
34.022.h3: 4. The Sevenfold Classification of Power Centers
34.024.p: Seven beings equal to the Supreme Power Directors, regulating the master energy circuits of the grand universe.
34.025.p: They work closely with the Seven Supreme Executives and act as high-level coordinators of universe power. [29:2.10]
34.027.p: One million power centers exist in Havona, each supervising one thousand worlds.
34.028.p: They represent perfect energy control, the ultimate goal for all power centers and physical controllers. [29:2.12]
34.030.p: Each superuniverse has 1,000 power centers organizing vast energy systems. They receive triple energy streams and distribute them into seven circuits, forming the electronic structure of universe power. [29:2.13]
34.032.p: Each local universe has 100 centers that reduce and adapt superuniverse energy for practical use.
34.033.p: They support constellations and systems, and help establish energy routes for communication. [29:2.16]
34.035.p: Ten centers in each constellation project energy to about 100 local systems. They supply power for communication, transport, and life support, but do not directly manage life.[29:2.17]
34.037.p: Each local system has one center that distributes energy to inhabited worlds. They coordinate physical controllers and ensure stable and efficient power flow. [29:2.18]
34.039.p: These rare centers function only in special situations, not on inhabited planets. They help maintain cosmic balance and appear only in very unusual energy conditions.[29:2.19]
34.040.h3: 5. The Seven Progressional Levels of Cosmic Energy
34.042.p: Primordial force is the unrevealed force-charge of space potentials under the presence and domain of the Unqualified Absolute before any organized energy manifestation appears[42:2.9].
34.044.p: This pre-energy stage, the transitional manifestation toward organized energy, is divided into two levels activated by the passive and then active action of the Primary Force Organizers toward emergent segregata and later gravita[42:2.10].
34.046.p: This segregated level of energy, directional and tense, is the first true form of force transformation before gravity responsiveness, representing vast mass-movement and system dominance[42:2.11].
34.048.p: This secondary form generates gravity response, carries universe power potential, and contains the elemental ancestry of all matter, indicating response both to absolute Paradise gravity and later to linear gravity inherent in electronic mass units[42:2.12].
34.050.p: Ultimata is the collective designation for all energy stages which have entered gravity responsiveness and are moving toward full physical organization and matter formation[42:2.13].
34.052.p: Universe power is the gravity-dominated, controllable, directive, superimposed energy phase from which physical structures may be organized and electronic formations begin to stabilize [42:2.14].
34.054.p: Ultimatonic units are transformed into electronic circuits through the manipulative skill of the Power Centers and Master Physical Controllers who control and integrate ultimatons into orbiting electronic systems as the basic units of organized matter while retaining supervision until atomic vortex activity limits their function [42:4.3].
34.057.p: Most matter in suns, planets, and spatial bodies arises from nebular wheels whose gas masses possess extraordinary energy potentials, much of which may be captured by suns and re-radiated as space energy emissions, forming the primary source of cosmic matter under natural evolution rather than direct acts of Power Directors [15:5.1].
34.058.h4: 2) Tenfold Classification of Stellar and Planetary Origins
34.059.p: The majority of superuniverse suns and planets are traced through ten major nebular evolutionary categories, including concentric ring contraction, whirling star ejection from mother wheels, and multiple other cosmic processes inherent to evolutionary space genesis rather than direct power organization[15:5.3]~4.
35.title: The Origins, Differences, and Effective Practice of Prayer and Worship
35.001.h3: 1. Origins and Evolution of Prayer and Worship
35.002.h4: 1) Biological and Natural Origins of Worship
35.003.p: Primitive religion is a product of biological origin and natural evolution, independent of moral or spiritual influences, and while higher animals experience fear, they lack imagination and thus have no religion; however, man created primitive religion through illusions based on fear [85:0.1]. The primitive form of worship appeared long before man formed complex concepts, and the objects of early worship consisted of things in nature, taking on an intellectual character [85:0.2]. Humans have successively worshipped stones, hills, plants, trees, animals, elements, and heavenly bodies, which originated from fear and awe regarding inexplicable natural phenomena [85:1.1], 85:2.1, 85:3.1, 85:4.1, 85:5.1. While nature worship seems to have arisen spontaneously in the human mind, in reality, the sixth adjutant spirit, the spirit of worship, constantly stimulated the human impulse to worship, leading animalistic fear into expressions of worship [85:7.1].
35.004.h4: 2) Evolutionary Process of Prayer and its Relation to Magic
35.005.p: Prayer as a function of religion evolved from non-religious monologue and dialogue expressions, and as primitive man gained self-consciousness, the potentials for social reaction and God-consciousness appeared [91:0.1]. Early prayer was not addressed to a deity but was merely a monologue or magical expression wishing for good luck; later, as concepts of ghosts and spirits developed, it was directed toward supernatural beings, reaching the level of genuine prayer [91:0.2], 91:0.3. Prayer did not evolve from magic but arose independently; magic is an attempt to adjust deity to conditions, whereas prayer is an effort to adjust the individual to the will of deity [91:8.2]. When man realized that gods could not be coerced by prayer, prayer changed from coercion to petition and requests for favor, and the truest prayer became a communion between man and his Maker [91:2.3].
35.007.p: Early prayer focused on seeking material benefits, but it gradually developed into ethical prayer [91:1.3]. Selfish and material prayers wherein the pray-er seeks to gain advantage over his fellows cannot be ethical and are incompatible with ethical religion [91:4.1]. Ethical prayer must not be a substitute for action but should stimulate action and serve as a guide for progressive efforts toward ideal goals for self-realization [91:4.2]. When prayer seeks nothing for oneself or one's fellows but only spiritual communion, such an attitude reaches the levels of true worship [91:4.3].
35.008.h3: 2. Essential Differences and Definitions of Prayer and Worship
35.009.h4: 1) Functional Differences between Prayer and Worship
35.010.p: Prayer can be likened to recharging the spiritual batteries of the soul, while worship can be compared to the act of tuning in the soul to catch the universe broadcasts of the Infinite Spirit of the Universal Father [144:4.8]. Prayer is the sincere looking of the child to the spirit Father and is a psychological process of exchanging the human will for the divine will [144:4.9]. When prayer is uplifted by the spirit, it leads to cooperative spiritual progress, and ideal prayer is a form of spiritual communion that leads to intelligent worship [144:2.2]. Prayer is a means to strengthen the self and seek help for better living and higher achievement, and it is a dual human experience that looks to the subconscious for material aid or to the superconscious for spiritual inspiration [91:3.5], 91:3.6.
35.011.h4: 2) Jesus’ Distinction between Prayer and Worship
35.012.p: Jesus was frequently alone on the mountain to have personal communion with the Father; it is not proper to describe this communion simply as prayer, nor is it consistent to speak of his worshipping, but it is entirely correct to refer to it as personal communion with the Father [144:1.8]. Jesus usually prayed in the plural, not the singular, and he prayed for himself only during the great crises of his earth life [144:4.6]. Through prayer, Jesus achieved supercommunion with the supreme rulers of the universe, and prayer leads earth mortals toward the communion of true worship [144:4.4]. Worship, as Jesus taught, is an experience that makes the worshiper increasingly like the being who is worshipped, and it is a transforming experience wherein the finite reaches the presence of the Infinite [146:2.17].
35.014.p: Solving Rodan viewed the isolation of Jesus' worshipful meditation not only as a technique for gathering wisdom and strength to resolve daily conflicts but also as a method for gaining energy to solve higher problems of a moral and spiritual nature [160:1.10]. This habit of worship brings a relaxation that renews the mind, inspires the soul, enables one to face problems courageously, and removes fear [160:1.12]. From the human standpoint, worship is a combination of meditation and relaxation; meditation allows the mind to contact the spirit, and relaxation determines the capacity for spiritual receptivity [160:3.1].
35.015.h3: 3. Principles and Conditions of Effective Prayer
35.016.h4: 1) Requirements for Effective Prayer Taught by Jesus
35.017.p: Jesus taught that effective prayer must be unselfish, based on faith, and sincere [144:3.17]~20. Furthermore, prayer must be wise and must trust in the Father’s wise will [144:3.21], 144:3.22. If injustice is persistently harbored in a person's heart, the prayer connection in the spiritual circuit between the human soul and the Creator is gradually severed [146:2.2]. Prayer that is contrary to the known laws of God is an abomination; thus, he who turns his ear away from hearing the divine law causes spiritual beings to close their ears to his prayers [146:2.3]. He who would receive mercy must show mercy, and while the sincerity of prayer is the assurance of its being heard, the spiritual wisdom and cosmic consistency of the prayer determine the time, manner, and degree of the answer [146:2.6].
35.018.h4: 2) The Relationship between Forgiveness and Prayer
35.019.p: God's forgiveness is not actually dependent on man forgiving his fellows, but in experience, it becomes realizable only when man forgives his fellows [146:2.4]. The synchronicity of divine forgiveness and human forgiveness was linked in the prayer Jesus taught his apostles with the phrase, "Forgive us our debts as we forgive our debtors" [144:3.9]~10. When you forgive your brother in the flesh, you thereby create the capacity in your own soul for the reception of the reality of God's forgiveness of your own misdeeds [170:2.23].
35.020.h4: 3) Laws and Attitudes of Valid Petition
35.021.p: For effective prayer, one must face the problems of cosmic reality honestly and courageously and possess cosmic endurance [91:9.2]. One must also honestly exhaust human capacity for human adjustment and make a sincere effort [91:9.3], and one must wholeheartedly select the divine will and abandon indecision [91:9.5]. Prayer should be focused on seeking divine wisdom to solve human problems and must possess living faith [91:9.7]~8. Jesus taught to avoid the danger of becoming self-centered in prayer and to pray more for the spiritual progress of one's brethren [146:2.10].
35.022.h3: 4. Practice and Results of True Prayer and Worship
35.023.h4: 1) Attitude and Practice of True Prayer
35.024.p: Prayer is entirely a personal and spontaneous expression of the attitude of the soul toward the spirit, and it is the breath of the soul [144:2.2]~3. Jesus taught his apostles to always pray in secret, to go into the quiet surroundings of nature or into a room, close the door, and dedicate themselves to prayer [144:3.14]. True prayer should always be private; while prayers of thanksgiving are appropriate in groups of worshipers, the prayer of the soul is a personal matter [146:2.12]. Jesus preferred spontaneous prayer over formal prayer, but in response to the apostles' request, he taught the model prayer beginning with "Our Father who is in heaven," which was a pattern for group or social prayer [144:3.2], 144:3.16.
35.025.h4: 2) Answers to Prayer and the Time Factor
35.026.p: When a prayer is seemingly unanswered, the delay often signifies a better answer, and a better answer has been provided from the superior viewpoint of the spiritual world [168:4.5]. Time prayers, inspired by the spirit and expressed in faith, are often so vast and all-encompassing that they can only be answered in eternity [168:4.6]. The answer to the prayer of the mortal mind is often of such a nature that it can be received and recognized only after that same praying mind has attained the immortal state [168:4.7]. As in the case of Lazarus, answers may be delayed or appear in a different form according to the divine plan, contrary to human temporal expectations [168:4.5].
35.027.h4: 3) The Essence of True Worship and Social Repercussions
35.028.p: The object of worship in true religion must be the divine reality of infinite values inherent in the spiritual reality of the Eternal God, and the religion of Jesus demands living spiritual experience [160:5.5], 160:5.12. When prayer becomes a feature of divine worship, its influence transcends all other conduct, leading to the cultivation of divine ideals [91:5.1]. Group or public prayer is effective because its repercussions are highly social, and when the group engages in community prayer for moral enhancement and spiritual uplift, the entire group is made better [91:5.2]. True worship is a transforming experience wherein the finite progressively approaches and ultimately attains the presence of the Infinite [146:2.17].
36.title: The Universal Unity: From the Infinite Source to the Trinity of Trinities
36.001.h3: 1. Origins of Unity: The I AM and Differentiation of Reality
36.003.p: The origin of all universal unity lies in the infinite 'I AM.' From the viewpoint of sequential time, all reality originates from this infinite I AM, who exists as the Infinite and as infinity itself [105:1.3]. In the primordial eternal state before reality existed, the I AM existed without differentiation of thing and no thing, cause and effect, will and response, but at a hypothetical eternal moment, the I AM laid the foundation for universal reality through self-metamorphosis, differentiating himself into deified reality and undeified reality, potential reality and actual reality [105:2.3]. Despite this differentiation, there is a fundamental unity in infinity, which is the most important philosophical assumption the creature mind must accept [115:3.3].
36.004.h4: 2) Emergence of the Seven Absolutes of Infinity
36.005.p: The self-differentiation of the I AM was eternalized as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity, which are the basis of reality, having no beginning and being eternal [105:3.1]. These Seven Absolutes consist of the Universal Father, the Eternal Son, the Infinite Spirit, the Isle of Paradise, the Deity Absolute, the Universal Absolute, and the Unqualified Absolute [105:3.2]-8. Among them, the Universal Father is the father of personality and the source of all reality, the Isle of Paradise is the source of undeified absolute patterns, and the Deity Absolute is the totality of all deity potentials [105:3.2]~6. These Seven Absolutes encompass all reality and represent the complete list of universal realities resulting from the differentiation of the I AM [104:3.5].
36.007.p: After the I AM differentiated into the Seven Absolutes, they functionally associate again to form Triunities to function on the stage of the universe [105:4.6]. The Seven Triunities are the functional balance wheels of infinity, unifying the uniqueness of the Seven Infinite Absolutes and enabling the Father-I AM to experience functional unity of infinity [104:4.46]. These associations cannot increase the infinitude of the Father, but they allow his reality to be expressed in subinfinite and subabsolute ways, deifying new meanings and values and revealing potentials [104:4.47].
36.008.h3: 2. Structural Basis of Universal Unity and Threefold Gravity
36.009.h4: 1) Absolute Unity of the Paradise Trinity
36.010.p: The core of the functional unity of the universe is the Paradise Trinity. Existing as the Deity union of the Father, Son, and Spirit, the Paradise Trinity is real, and these three eternal persons never violate the truth of the indivisibility of Deity [10:4.4], 1:7.8. While the Deities of the Trinity have distinct differences in their universe activities, they are absolutely equal in nature and coordinate in being, and when functioning as undivided Deity, they achieve perfect unity [10:3.4], 56:6.1. The Trinity unifies all levels of the universe through its attitude toward the finite (the Supreme), its attitude toward the absonite (the Ultimate), and its absolute attitude [10:5.4]-6.
36.011.h4: 2) Unity of Physical, Mindal, and Spiritual Energies
36.012.p: The unity of the universe is maintained through the perfect coordination of physical, mindal, and spiritual energies. Pure energy responds to the physical gravity centering on the Isle of Paradise, and all forms of force-energy originate from and are controlled by this center [56:1.3]. Mind is unified by the Infinite Spirit; the infinite and universal mind is adequately unified under the supervision of the Seven Master Spirits, who are in turn perfectly correlated with the all-embracing mind of the Infinite Spirit [56:2.3]. Spirit is centered by the spiritual gravity of the Eternal Son, and spirit must always and ultimately be threefold in expression and Trinity-unified in final realization [56:3.1], 56:3.6.
36.013.h4: 3) Unity of Personality and the Universal Father
36.014.p: Beyond physical, mindal, and spiritual gravities, personality inherently possesses the quality of unifying all constituent realities. The personality circuit centered in the person of God the Father on Paradise provides the perfect unification of the manifold expressions of divine personality regarding all creature personalities [56:4.2]~3. The infinite personality of the Universal Father unifies all seven constituent Absolutes of Infinity, and pure energy, pure spirit, and all other realities are one and unified in God [56:4.2], 56:1.4.
36.015.h3: 3. Evolutionary Unity and Realization of the Experiential Deity
36.016.h4: 1) Unity of the Supreme and the Finite
36.017.p: Throughout the evolving universes of time and space, the unity of Deity is a task to be achieved, and the Supreme Being functions as the unifier of time-space divinity and the maximum of Deity that finite creatures can actually comprehend [56:5.4], 56:8.1. The Supreme Being is the Oversoul of the grand universe, unifying the experiences of all evolving creatures and creators within his divine nature [117:1.1], 117:1.6. While the sovereignty of the Supreme is developing in time, the power of the Almighty Supreme depends on the divine acts of God the Sevenfold, and all experiences of man seeking God and striving to be like him are eternally preserved and unified in the Supreme Being [116:4.2], 117:5.12.
36.019.p: If the Supreme Being is responsible for the unification of the finite level, the Ultimate Being is the Deity who unifies realities on the transcendental level supervening the finite [105:7.3]. The Ultimate Being transcends time and space but is still an absonite being, possessing unique capacities for functional association with the Absolutes [106:4.4]. The Trinity Ultimate is an association of Deity consisting of the Supreme Creators, the Supreme Being, and the Architects of the Master Universe, destined to coordinate and unify the master creation [106:4.2].
36.020.h3: 4. Ultimate Re-integration: The Trinity of Trinities and Completion
36.021.h4: 1) Experiential Integration of Reality and the Absolute Triunity
36.022.p: The emergence of the Supreme Being and the Ultimate Being lays the foundation for the second experiential Trinity, the Trinity Absolute, which is the union of God the Sevenfold, God the Ultimate, and the Consummator of Universe Destiny [106:5.1]. The Trinity Absolute holds the theoretical capacity to activate the Absolutes of potentiality (Deity, Universal, and Unqualified Absolutes), and its function is anticipated to be truly absolute in total function [106:6.4]. The complete function of this Trinity will be finally expressed in the creations of infinity and completed in the absolute realization of all potentials [106:6.3].
36.023.h4: 2) The Trinity of Trinities and Realization of the Infinite
36.024.p: The climax of universal unity is the Trinity of Trinities. This is the union of the Paradise Trinity (existential), the Trinity Ultimate (experiential), and the Trinity Absolute (experiential), representing the actual summation of the entirety of experiential infinity [106:8.1]. Within the Trinity of Trinities, experiential infinity is identified with existential infinity, and both infinities become one in the pre-experiential existential I AM [106:8.1]. The union of these three Trinities includes causes, intermediates, and finals; it comprises beginnings, existences, and destinies, enabling the infinite integration of reality [106:8.12].
36.025.h4: 3) Return to the I AM and Perfect Unity
36.026.p: Just as the Universal Father initially existed alone as the I AM, in the future eternity, through vast changes on the experiential level, the concept of the I AM will signify full self-realization [106:8.23]. The Father-Son union expands to Son-Spirit, Spirit-Supreme, Supreme-Ultimate, Ultimate-Absolute, and Absolute-Father-Infinite, completing the cycle of reality and enabling the self-realization of the infinity of the primordial reality of the First Source and Center [106:8.12]. The Universal Father is the explanation for the ultimate unity of absolute values and meanings, universal unity that must be realized supremely in the unqualified reality [56:9.11].
37.title: Deity and Reality: Origin, Dimensions, and Integration
37.001.h3: 1. The I AM and the Origin and Differentiation of Reality
37.002.h4: 1) Concept of the I AM and Primordial Reality
37.003.p: Universe philosophers attribute the absolute first cause to the Universal Father functioning as the infinite, eternal, and absolute I AM [105:1.1]. From the sequential viewpoint of time, all reality has its origin in the infinite I AM, whose solitary existence in past infinite eternity must be the first philosophical postulate of the finite creature [105:1.3]. As an ontological concept, the I AM is neither deified nor undeified, neither actual nor potential, neither personal nor impersonal; no qualification can be applied to the Infinite except to state that the I AM is [105:1.4]. To explain the origin of reality, when a hypothetical moment of eternity is assumed, the I AM can be perceived as thing and no thing, as cause and effect, as will and response; at this moment, there is no differentiation throughout infinity [105:1.5]. Through the internal metamorphosis of the I AM, he initiates multiple differentiations into deified reality and undeified reality, potential reality and actual reality, which are realities absolutely revealed within the presence of the First Source and Center [105:2.3].
37.004.h4: 2) Emergence of the Seven Absolutes of Infinity
37.005.p: The seven prime relationships within the I AM eternalize as the Seven Absolutes of Infinity, which are the premise of reality and possess no beginning [105:3.1]. The First is the Universal Father as the source of all potential and actual, the Second is the Eternal Son as the Absolute Personality Reality, and the Third is the Conjoint Actor as the unifier of all actual and actualizing reality [105:3.2], 105:3.3, 105:3.5. The Fourth is the Paradise Source and Center as the pattern Absolute of nonpersonal reality, the Fifth is the Deity Absolute as the totality of all deity potential, the Sixth is the Unqualified Absolute as the totality of undeified reality and the space presence of infinite potential, and the Seventh is the Universal Absolute who unifies the deified and undeified and coordinates the absolute and relative [105:3.4], 105:3.6, 105:3.7, 105:3.8. These Seven Absolutes are the complete list of universal realities resulting from the differentiation of the I AM, and although they may seem sequential to the mortal mind, they are essentially coeternal [105:2.1], 105:3.10.
37.007.p: Unity begets duality, duality begets triunity, and triunity is the functional association of the seven Absolutes of Infinity which eternalizes the potential of all reality [105:4.3], 105:4.6~7. With the eternalization of triunity, the stage of the universe is set; potential reality becomes existent, reality becomes present, and the fullness of eternity witnesses the diversification of cosmic energy and the diffusion of Paradise spirit [105:4.9]. The union of the three Absolutes of actuality (Eternal Son, Infinite Spirit, Isle of Paradise) constitutes the actual revelation, while the union of the three Absolutes of potentiality (Deity, Unqualified, and Universal Absolutes) constitutes the potential revelation; their interassociation generates the tension in infinity that makes all universe growth possible [115:3.7]~9.
37.008.h3: 2. Universe Dimensions of Reality and Divine Manifestation
37.009.h4: 1) Dimensions of Finite, Absonite, and Absolute
37.010.p: To facilitate the comprehension of the universe of universes, the levels of universal reality are designated as finite, absonite, and absolute; only the absolute is unqualifiedly eternal and truly existential, while absonites and finites are derivatives, modifications, and qualifications of the original absolute reality [115:1.3]. The finite exists because the eternal purpose of God so willed it [115:1.4]. The promulgation of finite reality limits the absolute level and signifies the appearance of relativity, which is due to the volitional act of Paradise Deity and the adjustment of the functional triunities [105:5.1], 105:5.2. With the appearance of relative and limited reality, a new cycle of reality, a growth cycle, is initiated, which is a majestic descent from the heights of infinity to the domain of the finite [105:5.5].
37.011.h4: 2) Cosmic Function of Time and Space
37.012.p: Time and space are the conjoined mechanism of the master universe, devices that enable finite creatures to coexist in the universe with the Infinite, whereby creatures are effectively insulated from absolute levels [118:9.1]. Deity can unify time-space phenomena into finite concepts only by omnipresence, for time is a succession of instants while space is a system of associated points [118:3.1]. Time makes experience possible, and in the evolving universes, eternity is temporal everlastingness—the everlasting now [118:1.1]. Space is the nearest of all nonabsolute things to being absolute, and on material levels, space is also a property of all material bodies [118:3.5]~6. Every creature of the finite universe of time and space lives, moves, and has his being within the immanence of the Supreme Being [117:3.12].
37.014.p: Providence is the function of the impersonal overcontrol of the universe, extending from the evolutionary levels of the Sevenfold Deity, wherein the power of the Almighty is synthesized, to the transcendental realms of the Ultimate Deity [118:10.4]. True providence is the actual correlation and realization of the energies of space, the motions of time, the thoughts of intellect, the ideals of character, and the desires of spiritual nature, achieving final finite unification within the interrelated presence of the Supreme and the Ultimate [118:10.7]. Providence is partial because of the incompleteness of the actualization of the Supreme Being, and unpredictable due to the fluctuations in creature attitude, yet it is the sure and slow emergence of the mighty sovereign of the grand universes that evolving creatures detect in their universe progress [118:10.20]~23.
37.015.h3: 3. The Supreme Being and Evolutionary Integration of Finite Reality
37.016.h4: 1) Nature and Function of the Supreme Being
37.017.p: The Supreme Being is the Oversoul of the grand universe, the consciousness of the finite universe, the completion of finite reality, and the personification of creator-creature experience [117:1.1]. The Supreme Being is the actualizing Deity embodying the creative will that encompasses the evolving universe purpose, and his divine nature is composed of the vast mosaic of the total of the natures of all creatures and Creators [117:5.1]. God the Supreme is the God of time, holding the secret of creature growth in time within his presence, and the ultimate fruit of all finite growth is the Supreme Being [117:2.1]. The Supreme connects the finite and the absonite, integrating them through the process of summarizing evolutionary experience, much as the mind of the Conjoint Actor integrates spirituality and energy [115:7.8].
37.018.h4: 2) The Almighty Supreme and Power-Personality Integration
37.019.p: The Almighty Supreme is a living, evolving Deity of power and personality, and his present domain, the grand universe, is likewise a growing realm of power and personality [116:0.4]. The union of the power and personality attributes of Supremacy is the function of the Supreme Mind, and the completed evolution of the Almighty Supreme will result in one unified personal Deity [116:1.2]. The experiential power derived from the divine achievements of God the Sevenfold is synthesized and integrated as the almighty power, manifesting the cohesiveness of Deity, which then associates with the spirit personality of the Supreme Being on the pilot world of the outer belt of Havona worlds to form spirit-personality cohesiveness [106:2.4]. In the Supreme Being, Creators and creatures are united in one Deity, forever bound by the experience born of the common problems of the finite creation as they walk the eternal path from the fetters of imperfection toward perfection [117:1.6].
37.020.h4: 3) Mutual Dependence of Man and the Supreme
37.021.p: Man does not lose his personal identity by uniting with the Supreme Being, but the repercussions of all human experience in the universe form a part of the divine experience of the Supreme Being [117:5.5]. If a mortal man continues the Paradise adventure, he follows the flow of time within the current of eternity, and to the extent that the human ego refuses to participate in the Paradise ascent, the Supreme Being is delayed in achieving divine expression in the grand universe [117:4.11]. God the Supreme depends, in a sense, upon the choices of the mortal will, and the spiritualization and eternalization of personality in human evolution directly lead to the expansion of the sovereignty of the Supreme Being [117:4.9], 117:4.10. As human beings fulfill their destiny, the Supreme Being also fulfills his destiny on the level of Deity [117:4.12].
37.022.h3: 4. God the Ultimate and Attainment of Transcendental Reality
37.023.h4: 1) Transcendental Reality and God the Ultimate
37.024.p: Transcendental reality is subinfinite and subabsolute but superfinite and supercreative, manifesting as an integrating level correlating the supervalues of the absolute with the maximum values of the finite [105:7.1]. Just as the Supreme Being is associated with the finite, God the Ultimate is identified with transcendental reality, being something more than a super-Supreme projected on the transcendental level, appearing as a manifestation of new deity realities [105:7.3]. God the Ultimate is a being transcending time and space but remains a subabsolute being, despite possessing inherent capacity for functional association with the Absolutes [106:4.4]. Realities associated with the transcendental level include the divine presence of the Ultimate and the Architects of the Master Universe [105:7.5], 105:7.7.
37.025.h4: 2) The Trinity Ultimate and Integration of the Master Universe
37.026.p: The first experiential Trinity (the Trinity Ultimate), consisting of the union of the Supreme Creators, the Supreme Being, and the Architects of the Master Universe, is destined for the further integration of the evolving master creation [106:3.2]. This Trinity provides for the group attainment of ultimate objectives, and in the ages to come, the Corps of the Mortal Finality will proclaim the purposes of the Paradise Deities as determined by the Trinity Ultimate [106:3.4]. The Trinity Ultimate is destined to coordinate the master creation, and the complete eventuation of God the Ultimate signifies the completion of the master creation [106:4.2].
37.027.h3: 5. Final Integration of Reality and the Trinity of Trinities
37.028.h4: 1) Absolute Integration and the Trinity Absolute
37.029.p: The actual emergence of the Ultimate and the Supreme lays the foundation for the second experiential Trinity, the Trinity Absolute, which is the union of God the Sevenfold, God the Ultimate, and the Consummator of Universe Destiny [106:5.1]. This Trinity possesses the theoretical capacity to activate the Absolutes of potentiality (Deity, Universal, and Unqualified Absolutes) and is anticipated to be truly absolute in total function [106:5.1], 106:6.4. The complete function of the Trinity Absolute will be finally expressed in the creations of infinity and consummated in the absolute realization of all potentials [106:6.3].
37.030.h4: 2) The Trinity of Trinities and Realization of the Infinite
37.031.p: The Trinity of Trinities is the union of the Paradise Trinity (existential), the Trinity Ultimate (experiential), and the Trinity Absolute (experiential), representing the actual summation of the entirety of experiential infinity [106:8.1]. Within the Trinity of Trinities, experiential infinity is identified with existential infinity, and both infinities are unified in the pre-experiential existential I AM [106:8.1]. This union encompasses causes, intermediates, and finals, comprising beginnings, existences, and destinies, enabling the infinite integration of reality [106:8.12].
37.032.h4: 3) Return to the I AM and Final Destiny
37.033.p: Just as the Universal Father initially existed alone as the I AM, in the future eternity, through vast changes on the experiential level, the concept of the I AM will signify full self-realization [106:8.23]. We conclude that when the second level of the Trinity of Trinities achieves unification, it will lead directly to the experiential attainment of the I AM, and the final destiny of all personalities is the final knowing of the Universal Father of these selfsame personalities [106:8.22]. In the present universe moment of existence, the unqualified unity of infinity integrates all diversity of reality in absolute existential majesty, and this will be consummated by the integration of infinity as experiential reality [106:9.1].
38.title: Finaliters: Origin, Composition, and Universal Destiny
38.002.h4: 1) Origin of Mortal Finaliters and Adjuster Fusion
38.003.p: The Corps of Mortal Finaliters is the present known destiny of the ascending mortals of time who have fused with the Adjuster [31:0.1]. Evolutionary planets are spheres of human origin, and worlds like Urantia are the starting points, where you and your divine Thought Adjuster are joined in temporary union [112:0.1]. If man runs the race of time faithfully and reaches the final goal of faith, he will be eternally fused with his indwelling Adjuster, and this fusion is the mystery of making God and man one and an eternally true fact [112:0.1], 112:7.2. From the moment of Adjuster fusion, the status of the ascender is that of the evolutionary creature, and the human supersedes the Adjuster in all matters regarding personality, categorized as an ascending mortal on the whole trip to the Corps of the Finality as a unique union of God and man [112:7.12].
38.004.h4: 2) Essential Meaning and Status of Finaliters
38.005.p: Finaliters are the true tested souls of time and space, the evolutionary salt of the earth, and are forever proof against evil and safe from sin [31:0.13]. Although mortal man is of animal origin and his body is dust, if he truly desires, he has the heritage of ages and will someday serve throughout the universes as a true son of the Paradise Father and the Supreme God of experience [112:7.19]. They have fully obeyed the mandate of the ages to "Be you perfect," have found God, and have been duly inducted into the Corps of the Finality, having achieved the present limit of creature perfection and experienced the fullness of Deity worship [31:3.6]. Finaliters take oath of allegiance only to the Paradise Trinity and constitute a fully self-governing body, influenced by no outside pressure [31:0.12].
38.006.h4: 3) Purpose of Forming the Corps of Finality
38.007.p: The plan of the Paradise Father is to bestow himself upon finite creatures and to endow them eternally with divinity, and with Adjuster fusion, this promise is completed [112:7.14]. The Corps of Finality is organized in accordance with the working associations of the worlds of space and in keeping with the associative experience acquired throughout the long and eventful ascending career [31:0.9]. This group goes back to serve in the universes of time in the present universe age and is assigned to labor in other superuniverses, never in their native superuniverse until they have finished service in all seven, possibly to acquire the sevenfold concept of the Supreme Being [31:0.10].
38.008.h3: 2. Composition and Types of the Corps of Finality
38.009.h4: 1) Members of the Primary Corps of Finality
38.010.p: While the Corps of Mortal Finaliters is the core of the primary corps, other groups are also assigned to it [31:0.1]. This corps consists of six groups of glorified beings: Havona Natives, Gravity Messengers, Glorified Mortals, Adopted Seraphim, Glorified Material Sons, and Glorified Midway Creatures [31:0.2], 31:0.3, 31:0.4, 31:0.5, 31:0.6, 31:0.7. All ascending humans admitted to this group are treated as equals, but this exalted equality does not abrogate personality or destroy personal identity, and one can immediately discern the origin of a finaliter when communicating with them [31:0.9].
38.012.p: Havona Natives are perfect beings created by Deity, and they are admitted to the corps at a ratio of one to every company of one thousand finaliters to provide the viewpoint of the perfect-born [31:1.1], 31:1.3. Gravity Messengers are modified and personalized Adjusters possessing the ability to transcend time and space, and they are assigned only to the primary Corps of Finality, functioning under the command of Grandfanda [31:2.1], 31:2.2. One Gravity Messenger is attached to each company of finaliters, and they cherish a deep affection for the glorified mortal finaliters because both share a fragment of the Universal Father [31:2.3], 31:2.4.
38.014.p: Ascending Adjuster-fused mortals compose the bulk of the primary Corps of Finality, usually constituting 990 in each finaliter company along with adopted seraphim [31:3.1]. Many of the faithful seraphic guardians of mortals fuse with the Father and then join their human subjects to take the finaliter oath of eternity, being mustered into this Corps of Finality forever as equals on the basis of adoption [31:4.1]. Only guardians of destiny are mustered into the primary Corps of Mortal Finaliters, and they achieve spiritual bi-unification on Seraphington before entering the finaliter corps, gaining the capacity to fuse with a non-Adjuster fragment of the Paradise Father [113:7.8].
38.016.p: Some Material Sons (Adams and Eves) who have failed or were delayed in their planetary missions undergo the process of ascending by being humanized, receiving Adjusters, passing through death, and reaching the Corps of Finality [31:5.2]. Glorified midway creatures are also released from their permanent citizenship status to ascend to Paradise, and all secondary midwayers are mustered into the Corps of Finality after fusing with Adjusters [31:6.1], 31:6.2.
38.018.p: Besides the Corps of Mortal Finaliters, there are six other corps of finaliters supervised by the Senior Master Architect [31:10.1]. These are the Corps of Paradise Finaliters, the Corps of Trinitized Finaliters, the Corps of Conjoint Trinitized Finaliters, the Corps of Havona Finaliters, the Corps of Transcendental Finaliters, and the Corps of Unrevealed Sons of Destiny [31:10.~8]. The gathering of these seven finaliter corps signifies the activation of potentials transcending even the future master universe functions of the Supreme Being and probably signifies the present activity of the Ultimate Trinity engaged in dominating the forces of the finite and the absonite in preparation for inconceivable developments in the universes of space [31:10.10].
38.020.h4: 1) Stages of Fusion and Spiritual Progress
38.021.p: To become a finaliter, the human soul must have ample opportunity to reveal its true intention and real purpose, and must fuse with the spiritual reality to eventually attain the status of spirit reality [112:5.9], 112:2.20. From the moment of fusion with the Adjuster, the personality is safe from danger in the eternal career, and it receives authorization for fusion from the superuniverse government to qualify for the journey toward Havona and Paradise [112:7.4], 112:7.5. Humans become fourth-stage or graduate spirits after reaching the sixth circle of Havona, become fifth-stage spirits upon finding the Universal Father, and attain the sixth stage of spirit existence upon taking the oaths that enlist them forever in the mortal Corps of the Finality [31:3.4].
38.023.p: The glorified humans of the Paradise Corps of Finality are beings who have been trained to the limit of capacity to respect every detail of every divine principle of just and efficient administration, as well as the merciful and patient administration of all universe creation of time and space, during the ages from the lowest material worlds to the spiritual heights of Paradise [31:3.7]. They are the tested and tried souls of time and space, and are forever proof against evil and safe from sin [31:0.13]. They possess experiential knowledge of every step of the actuality of the life of intelligent beings and of every phase of their philosophy [31:3.7].
38.024.h3: 4. Role and Universal Destiny of Finaliters
38.026.p: In the present universe age, finaliters maintain headquarters on Paradise, in the superuniverses, in the local universes, and on all the divisional capitals, going back to serve in the universes of time and ministering throughout the universes of space [31:0.12], 31:0.8, 31:0.10. There is always one company or more of mortal finaliters in service on Urantia, and they alternate between assigned duty and free service [31:0.11]. Finaliters are the children of the Supreme Being, personalized and humanized Adjusters and adjusterized and eternalized mortals, functioning as administrators of the universe as the combination of the highest known expression of the essence of the First Source and Center and the lowest form of finite intelligence creation [112:7.18].
38.027.h4: 2) Relationship with the Supreme Being and Spiritual Compensation
38.028.p: Finaliters are the experiential children of the Supreme Being [112:7.16], and while man does not lose his personal identity by uniting with the Supreme, the repercussions of human experience in the universe form a part of the divine experience of the Supreme Being [117:5.5]. The finaliters who have participated in the evolution of the Supreme Deity during the present universe age will serve in the future eternity in an effort to compensate for the experiential deficiency of the outer universes in not participating in the time-space evolution of the Supreme Being [31:10.13]. Finaliters will also reveal the divinity and nature of God the Supreme to the future seventh-stage finaliters, which will serve the same role as the revelation of the Infinite to the Absolute serves for finite creatures [117:6.18].
38.030.p: The belief on Uversa is that the Corps of the Finality is destined for some future service in the universe space where we can already confirm the clustering of at least seventy thousand aggregations of matter [31:10.19]. We believe that the Adjuster-fused mortals, together with their finaliter associates, are destined to function as administrators in the universes of the first outer space level, and we have no doubt that when vast galaxies become inhabitable universes, among their administrators will be the Paradise finaliters [112:7.17]. The seven finaliter corps represent the divinity response of the grand universe to the future needs of the undeveloped potentials in the outer universes of future eternal activities [31:10.10], and they will be the superb leaders and matchless administrators there [112:7.18].
39.title: The Status and Bestowal Process of Christ Michael
39.001.h3: 1. Identity of Christ Michael and Origin and Purpose of Bestowals
39.002.h4: 1) Nature of Paradise Sons and Motive for Bestowal
39.003.p: Christ Michael is the creator and sovereign of the local universe of Nebadon, the 611,121st bestowal of the Eternal Son upon the universes of time and space, reflecting the divine nature of his Paradise parents [119:0.7]. Inherent in Paradise Sons is the desire to come close to the life experiences of their subordinate living creatures, a practice initiated by the Eternal Son's seven bestowals on the seven circuits of Havona [119:0.2]. When a Creator Son organizes and controls a new universe, he solemnly swears to the Eternal Trinity not to assume full sovereignty until his seven creature bestowals have been successfully completed and certified by the Ancients of Days of his superuniverse [119:0.3]. Through these creature incarnations, the Creators are educated to become wise, compassionate, and just sovereigns, gaining understanding mercy through these experiences despite being inherently just [119:0.4]. These bestowals are not essential for efficient universe management but are absolutely necessary for the just and merciful administration of a universe filled with imperfect creatures [119:0.5].
39.004.h4: 2) Essential Process for Acquiring Sovereignty and Embodiment of Divine Will
39.005.p: Although Michael Sons begin universe organization with fairness and sympathy toward the various beings they have created, the Ancients of Days will not certify a Creator Son as universe sovereign until he has truly acquired the viewpoint of his creatures by actual experience in their environment [119:0.6]. Michael did not wish to rule Nebadon in his own right as a Creator Son but desired to ascend to high universe status through the actual experience of cooperative subordination to the Paradise Trinity [120:0.3]. During each universe bestowal, Michael successfully subordinated himself to the will of the various associations of the Paradise Trinity persons, thereby causing his sovereignty to embody the sevenfold viewpoint of Paradise Deities and the viewpoint of time-space creatures simultaneously [120:0.5]. The Creator Son needed no instructions to execute this incarnation for the sole purpose of achieving universe sovereignty, but he chose to function in cooperation with the various wills of the Paradise Deities to embark on a program of revealing the Supreme [120:0.7].
39.006.h3: 2. History of the Seven Bestowals in Nebadon
39.007.h4: 1) Summary of First through Sixth Bestowals
39.008.p: Michael's first bestowal occurred about one billion years ago in the likeness of a Melchizedek Son, where he lived as a Melchizedek, performed 24 universe emergency missions, and became the chief of the Melchizedeks [119:1.1], 119:1.4, 119:1.5. The second bestowal was in the likeness of a Lanonandek Son, where he ruled for over 17 years as acting System Sovereign in System 11 of Constellation 37, replacing the rebel Lutentia and bringing order to a confused system [119:2.1], 119:2.4, 119:2.5. The third bestowal was in the likeness of a Material Son on Planet 217 of Constellation 61, where he functioned in isolation for a generation to achieve planetary rehabilitation following the second rebellion in Nebadon [119:3.1], 119:3.4. The fourth bestowal was in the likeness of a seraphim, where he served for about 40 years as a counselor to 26 master teachers, becoming "tested and tried in all points like as the seraphic personality" [119:4.3]~4. The fifth bestowal was in the likeness of a spirit mortal pilgrim on Uversa, the headquarters of the superuniverse of Orvonton, where he functioned for 11 years as a fully developed and trained spirit mortal [119:5.1]~3. The sixth bestowal was in the likeness of a morontia mortal on Endantum, the headquarters planet of the fifth constellation, showing that the universe sovereign had become a friend and sympathetic helper to the lowest form of created intelligence in his realm [119:6.1], 119:6.4.
39.009.h4: 2) Seventh Bestowal: Mortal Incarnation on Urantia
39.010.p: Michael's seventh and final bestowal took place on Urantia in the likeness of mortal flesh, choosing to appear as a helpless babe rather than a fully developed individual as in previous bestowals [119:7.2]~3. For this bestowal, Michael delegated all his universe authority to Immanuel and received counsel and instructions regarding the bestowal from Immanuel just before leaving for the Urantia incarnation [120:0.6]. In this bestowal, Michael chose to subject himself wholly to the will of the Universal Father, voluntarily forfeiting all extraplanetary support and special assistance to depend exclusively on the Paradise Father [120:1.2], 120:1.3. The Jewish baby Joshua ben Joseph (Jesus) was the incarnation of Michael of Nebadon, born of woman and reared in the ordinary manner of the children of that race and age [119:7.5], 119:7.7. Jesus' parents were average people of their day, and the only supernatural event associated with his birth was the announcement to the Chaldean priests by seraphims [119:7.6], 119:7.7.
39.011.h3: 3. Instructions for Urantia Bestowal and Mission of Jesus
39.012.h4: 1) Principles and Limitations Presented by Immanuel
39.013.p: Immanuel counseled Michael to concern himself only with the unbroken communion between him and the Paradise Father during the Urantia bestowal [120:1.4]. Michael was warned that while being an ordinary human of the realm, he would remain potentially a Creator Son, so he must refrain from formulating a superhuman will using his creative prerogatives and avoid exercising superhuman influence apart from the will of the Paradise Father [120:2.9]. He was to live according to the customs of family and community life of that time and generation, avoiding entanglements in the economic structure or political commitments of his day, and dedicating himself to living the ideal religious life [120:3.3]~4. Furthermore, he was not to interfere with the normal evolution of the Urantia races, to avoid the establishment of organized cults or stereotyped religious systems, and to ensure his life and teachings became the common heritage of all peoples [120:3.5], 120:3.6.
39.014.h4: 2) End of Rebellion and Mission of Spiritual Liberation
39.015.p: Michael was charged with the task of technically terminating the Lucifer rebellion in the system of Satania, achieving this through faith-submission to the Father's will in the weakness of mortal flesh [120:2.2]. He was to judge the blasphemous pretensions of Caligastia and Lucifer and forever end the lying of these fallen children of light, thereby practically clearing up the discord remaining in the universe [120:2.2]. Michael was primarily to function as a teacher to liberate man's spiritual nature, illuminate darkened human intellects, heal souls, and emancipate minds from fear [120:2.5]. Also, through his life in the flesh on Urantia, he was to be an inspiration to all lives on all Nebadon worlds for all generations to come, demonstrating the process of God seeking man and man finding God [120:2.7]~8.
39.017.p: Immanuel advised Michael to leave no writing upon the planet on permanent materials and to enjoin his associates to make no images of him, ensuring nothing potentially idolatrous remained [120:3.7]. While living as a normal male individual, he was not to enter into marriage relations, a restriction due to the mandate of Sonarington forbidding a bestowal Son of Paradise origin from leaving human offspring on a planet [120:3.8]. These instructions were intended to prevent the creation of stereotyped systems of Urantia religious beliefs and nonprogressive religious loyalties [120:3.7].
39.018.h3: 4. Completion of Bestowal, Results, and Nature of Jesus
39.019.h4: 1) Establishment of Sovereignty and Revelation of the Supreme
39.020.p: After successfully completing his final bestowal on Urantia, Michael was accepted by the Ancients of Days as the sovereign ruler of Nebadon and acknowledged by the Universal Father as the established head [119:8.1]. The completion of these seven bestowals not only brought supreme sovereignty to Michael but also created the possibility for the sovereignty of God the Supreme in Nebadon and constituted a new revelation of the Supreme Being [119:8.5]. By completing his creature bestowals, Michael advanced the sovereignty of the evolving God the Supreme and achieved a diversity of will revealing the will of the Supreme Being beyond merely exploring the nature of creature personalities [119:8.3]. Through the seven bestowals, Michael experienced everything from partial expression to the supremacy of full action, forever identifying himself with the Supreme Being [119:8.7].
39.021.h4: 2) Nature of Jesus: Union of God and Man
39.022.p: Christ Michael was a being of dual origin but not a double personality; he was not God in association with man but rather God incarnate in man [120:4.2]. Jesus did not become God at some moment in his earthly life; he was forever and always God and man, and just as the Paradise Trinity is one Deity, he was one [120:4.3]. Jesus of Nazareth was a miraculous person, yet he chose to manifest himself in the ordinary and natural method of divine action throughout all his extraordinary experiences [120:4.5]~6. The supreme spiritual purpose of the Urantia bestowal was to enhance the revelation of God, and Urantia has now become the sentimental shrine of Nebadon and the mortal home of Christ Michael [120:4.4], 119:8.8.
40.title: The Birth and Childhood of Jesus
40.001.h3: 1. Preparation for Bestowal and Selection of Parents
40.002.h4: 1) Background of Location and Parent Selection
40.003.p: After choosing Urantia as the planet for his final bestowal, Michael conferred with Gabriel and selected the Hebrews as the bestowal race [122:0.2]. Based on a report from a commission sent to investigate Jewish family life, Gabriel personally selected Joseph and Mary as the parents for Michael’s incarnation [122:0.3]. Joseph was a Hebrew, but he had many non-Jewish racial strains in his ancestry and was not a direct descendant of the line of David and Solomon, while Mary was culturally Jewish but genetically a composite of Syrian, Hittite, Phoenician, Greek, and Egyptian stocks, descending from a line of common but rugged ancestors [122:1.1]~2. Since it was Michael’s plan to appear as a common man and be understood by the common people, Gabriel selected Joseph and Mary because they possessed the most ideal combination of widespread racial connections and a superior average personality endowment [122:1.3].
40.004.h4: 2) Gabriel’s Visits and Announcement of Conception
40.005.p: The life work of Jesus was actually initiated by John the Baptist, and Gabriel first appeared to Elizabeth to announce that she would bear a son named John [122:2.1], 122:2.3. Subsequently, Gabriel appeared to Mary to announce that she would bear a son to be named Joshua, who would inaugurate the kingdom of heaven [122:3.1]. Mary pondered this supernatural visitation in her heart and later visited Elizabeth to gain assurance, while Joseph also became convinced through a dream that the child Mary would bear was to become a great light in the world [122:3.2], 122:4.1. throughout all these visitations, nothing was said about the house of David or a political Messiah of the Jews, but rather that Jesus was to be the Savior of the world for all nations [122:4.2].
40.007.h4: 1) Birth in Bethlehem and the Magi
40.008.p: Due to the census order by Rome, Joseph and Mary traveled to Bethlehem, and on August 21, 7 B.C., at noon, Mary gave birth to a male child and laid him in a manger [122:7.1], 122:8.1. When Jesus was born, the seraphim of Urantia sang anthems of glory, though they were not heard by human ears, and it was not shepherds but priests from Ur in Mesopotamia who visited the babe about three weeks later [122:8.5]~6. The legend of the star guiding the Wise Men to Bethlehem was a beautiful myth created later, based on the astronomical fact of a conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn [122:8.7].
40.009.h4: 2) Herod’s Persecution and Flight to Egypt
40.010.p: King Herod, having heard about a new king from the priests of Ur, became suspicious and ordered the slaughter of all male children in Bethlehem under two years of age [122:10.1], 122:10.3. However, Joseph and Mary were warned in advance through Zacharias and fled with Jesus to Alexandria, Egypt, around the middle of October, 6 B.C. [122:10.4]. They remained in Alexandria for two years with the help of kinsmen, during which time Jesus grew normally in health and Joseph gained experience working as a construction supervisor [123:0.1], 123:0.3.
40.012.h4: 1) Return to Nazareth and Early Home Education
40.013.p: After Herod’s death, Joseph and Mary returned to Nazareth in early October, 4 B.C., and Jesus, being a little over three years old, stood the trip well [123:0.6], 123:1.1, 123:1.2. According to the custom of Galilean Jews, Mary was responsible for his education until he was five, after which Joseph assumed responsibility for his intellectual and religious training [123:2.13]~14. Mary taught Jesus household tasks and how to care for vines, and in a sand box on the housetop, he learned Aramaic, Greek, and Hebrew [123:2.14]. On February 11, 2 B.C., when Jesus reached the age of moral decision, a Thought Adjuster came to indwell him [123:2.1].
40.014.h4: 2) School Life and Broad Understanding of Humanity
40.015.p: At seven years of age, Jesus entered the synagogue school in Nazareth to begin his study of the Book of the Law and the Prophets in Hebrew, distinguishing himself with his aptitude for languages [123:5.1], 123:5.9. In addition to formal schooling, Jesus mingled with caravans passing through Nazareth, contacting various human natures, and gained a wide practical knowledge through conversations with people visiting Joseph’s shop [123:5.6], 123:5.8. While he received moral and religious training at home and in the synagogue, his real education came from his association with his fellow men and his understanding and love for them [123:5.8].
40.017.p: As Jesus grew, he asked constant questions about natural phenomena, religious customs, and scientific facts, often perplexing his parents and teachers [123:6.6]. At age six, he was shocked by a mild earthquake to learn that his father did not know everything, and he startled his parents by insisting on talking to his Father in heaven rather than Joseph during prayer [123:3.2], 123:3.6. At age nine, he clashed with the school elders over making images out of clay, which was forbidden by law, but he eventually desisted from artistic activities in deference to his father’s wishes [124:1.4], 124:1.5. When visiting the gentile city of Scythopolis at age eleven, he was enthusiastic about the Greek amphitheater and games, suggesting they be introduced in Nazareth, which met with vehement opposition from Joseph [124:3.7], 124:3.8.
40.018.h3: 4. Self-Awareness and the Dawning of Mission
40.019.h4: 1) Awareness of Mission and Role in the Family
40.020.p: In his tenth year, in the month of July, Jesus first expressed feelings indicating he was becoming self-conscious of the unusual nature of his life mission, and the revelation of his divine identity and earthly mission gradually grew in his consciousness [124:2.1]. At age eleven, due to his mother’s illness and the birth of a brother, he was forced to assume the heavy responsibilities of the eldest son, moving from a childlike attitude to functioning as the practical head of the household [124:3.4]. Jesus was devoted to caring for and teaching his siblings and particularly loved music, entertaining his family with harp playing and singing [123:6.5], 124:4.3.
40.021.h4: 2) Conflict with Parents and Inner Struggle
40.022.p: Around the age of twelve, Jesus began to keenly sense a difference in viewpoint with his parents regarding the nature of his mission, feeling particularly burdened by Mary’s expectation of him as a political Messiah [124:4.5]. He questioned religious formalism and protested the custom of kissing the parchment on the doorpost, causing Joseph to remove it [124:4.7]. Jesus suffered great mental distress between the urge to be loyal to his own high convictions and the conscientious admonition to be submissive to his parents, but he eventually learned to harmonize these two by establishing a concept of group solidarity based on loyalty, fairness, and love [124:4.9].
40.023.h4: 3) Visit to Jerusalem and Assumption of Universal Responsibility
40.024.p: In A.D. 7, having reached the age of thirteen, Jesus graduated from the synagogue school and traveled to Jerusalem with his parents to attend his first Passover as a "son of the commandment" [124:6.1]. In Jerusalem, he was deeply impressed by the temple yet questioned the slaughter of countless animals for sacrifice, feeling compassion for the spiritually ignorant multitudes [124:6.14]~15. On the night before the Passover Sabbath, a messenger from Salvington appeared to Jesus saying, "The hour has come; it is time that you began your Father's business," marking a momentous transition where he began to shoulder the responsibilities of the universe even while living a life in the flesh [124:6.15], 124:6.16.
41.title: The Youth and Young Adulthood of Jesus
41.001.h3: 1. First Visit to Jerusalem and Shock at the Temple
41.002.h4: 1) The Reality of the Temple and Moral Indignation
41.003.p: Throughout Jesus' entire earth life, there was no incident more exciting and humanly thrilling than his visit to Jerusalem, and this remained in his memory as a great event of his childhood and early youth [125:0.1]. Jesus had held high expectations with a reverent heart toward the temple, but he suffered a great disillusionment upon entering the sacred gates, and he was particularly resentful of the fact that his mother was separated and could not accompany him to the consecration because she was a woman [125:0.4]. As he walked about the temple courts, he was shocked by the irreverence and the commercial noise, and he felt moral indignation at the sight of frivolous harlots [125:1.1], [125:1.2].
41.005.p: Above all, Jesus was shocked by the sight of the sacrificial offerings; the blood-stained pavement and the sounds of the dying animals were more than the nature-loving lad could bear [125:1.4]. He became convinced that his Father in heaven was not pleased with this slaughter of sacrifices, and he determined that someday he would celebrate a bloodless Passover [125:2.3]. During the Passover week, Jesus asked bold questions in a manner becoming his years, which somewhat nonplused the doctors of the law [125:4.3], and he poured out searching questions regarding the reality of the Holy of Holies, the discrimination against women, and the justification of animal sacrifice [125:5.3]~5.
41.006.h4: 3) The Father's Business and Awareness of Mission
41.007.p: When his parents discovered he was missing on their return trip and found him in the temple after three days, in response to his mother's reproach, Jesus replied, "Why is it that you have so long sought me? Would you not expect to find me in my Father’s house since the time has come when I should be about my Father’s business?" revealing an awareness of his mission [125:6.7]. Upon returning to Nazareth, Jesus pledged that while he must do the will of his Father in heaven, he would also be obedient to his father on earth and await his hour [125:6.11].
41.008.h3: 2. The Ordeal of Age 14 and the Death of Joseph
41.009.h4: 1) Historical Contemplation and Expectation of Miracles
41.010.p: The fourteenth and fifteenth years of Jesus were the most crucial in his earth life, and these two years, when he began to become self-conscious of divinity and destiny, were a time of great testing and temptation [126:0.1]. In his fourteenth year, Jesus climbed to the top of the hill of Simeon to meditate on Nazareth and the surrounding history, gradually becoming self-conscious of the nature of his bestowal on earth [126:1.1], [126:1.2]. His parents expected him to perform miracles to prove his calling, but as Jesus performed no such wonders, their confusion and anxiety grew [126:1.5].
41.011.h4: 2) Responsibility as Head of Household and Abandonment of Education
41.012.p: Just when the future of the family seemed bright, a tragedy occurred on September 25 when his father Joseph died in an accident while working on a construction job [126:2.1]. This event shattered Jesus' plans for education in Jerusalem, and at the tender age of fourteen, he assumed the responsibility as the head of the household, caring for his widowed mother and seven brothers and sisters [126:2.2]. Jesus willingly accepted this responsibility, and by not having to study with the rabbis, he entered the path of fulfilling the Father's mission without deriving authority for teaching truth from human sources [126:2.3].
41.014.p: Jesus early demonstrated sharp business judgment and financial wisdom, proving himself to be a wise manager of his father's estate [126:2.7]. While he did not entirely neglect the recreational side of life, he devoted increasing time and energy to two purposes: the care of his family and the preparation for doing his Father's will on earth [126:2.5].
41.015.h3: 3. Spiritual Awareness at Age 15 and Deepening Poverty
41.016.h4: 1) Birth of Ruth and Prototype of the Lord's Prayer
41.017.p: In his fifteenth year, the youngest child, Ruth, was born, and Jesus loved and nurtured baby Ruth with devotion, taking the place of his father Joseph [126:3.2]. During this year, Jesus first formulated the prayer that would later become known as "The Lord's Prayer" for the use of his family [126:3.3]. He reasoned that the support of his family must become his first duty, putting aside the visit to Jerusalem or his own plans [126:3.5].
41.018.h4: 2) 'Son of Man' Title and Establishing Identity
41.019.p: Jesus read the "Book of Enoch" in the Nazareth synagogue and was deeply impressed by the term "Son of Man" found therein [126:3.6]. He considered the Jewish concept of the Messiah but was convinced he was not to be a king leading armies or the Son of Man described by Daniel; he decided to adopt the "Son of Man" from the Book of Enoch as his inaugural title [126:3.8]. He knew he was not the Jewish Messiah, but his mother Mary still clung to the hope that he would restore the throne of David, causing Jesus to feel a sense of inner isolation.
41.021.p: On the first Sabbath after his fifteenth birthday, Jesus stood in the synagogue pulpit and read from Isaiah, revealing for the first time in public a solemn and authoritative demeanor regarding his mission [126:4.1], [126:4.8]. As the family finances became difficult, Jesus had to present his cherished copy of the Greek scriptures to the synagogue library to prevent it from being seized by tax collectors [126:5.6]. When Herod Antipas refused to pay the money owed to Joseph, Jesus gave up his dream of moving to a farm in the country and developed a distrust for the unjust ruler [126:5.7], [126:5.11].
41.022.h3: 4. Political Pressure of Youth and Leadership within the Family
41.023.h4: 1) Physical Growth and Awareness of Isolated Messiahship
41.024.p: In his sixteenth year, Jesus attained full physical growth, possessing a charming personality where the two natures of the human and the divine were harmonized [127:1.2]. Knowing he could not be the expected Jewish Messiah, he gradually ceased discussing his mission with his mother or family [127:1.7].
41.025.h4: 2) Temptation of the Zealots and Wise Refusal
41.026.p: In his seventeenth year, a nationalist rebellion known as the Zealots arose, and pressure was put on the youth of Nazareth to join [127:2.1]. Jesus' mother, uncle, and even his brother James urged him to join the nationalist movement, but Jesus wisely refused, citing his economic and moral duty to his family as paramount, leaving the memorable saying, "Money cannot love" [127:2.8]. This incident divided the sentiment of the people of Nazareth, and Jesus never again enjoyed universal favor [127:2.10].
41.028.p: In his eighteenth year, Jesus took his brother James to the Passover, attempting to show him the reality of the temple, but James did not react as sensitively as Jesus had [127:3.5]. At nineteen, Jesus persuaded his mother to change the family discipline from the negative taboos of "You shall not" to the positive mandate of "Do good" [127:4.2]. He showed the traits of a wise head of household, such as administering fair punishment through the consensus of the siblings when his brother Jude broke the rules [127:4.3]. Poverty continued, and Jesus had to sell his harp to pay for school expenses [127:4.10].
41.029.h3: 5. Entering Adulthood: Rejection of Love and New Spiritual Rituals
41.031.p: Rebecca, the daughter of a wealthy merchant, confessed her love and proposed to Jesus, but he politely refused, citing his duty to support his family and his destined mission [127:5.5]. Jesus made it clear that he could not enter into relations with any woman other than simple friendship, and Rebecca followed him devotedly all her life, never marrying another [127:5.6]. After this event, the affection of the people for Jesus took on more of the nature of respect and worship rather than personal possessiveness [127:6.1].
41.032.h4: 2) Bloodless Passover and Decision for Celibacy
41.033.p: In his twentieth year, while spending Passover at the home of Lazarus, Jesus celebrated a new Passover ritual for the first time, commemorating it with bread and wine instead of killing a lamb [127:6.7]. He taught that the Father in heaven did not desire animal sacrifice, and established the custom of celebrating this sacrament whenever he visited Bethany [127:6.7]. When Mary asked if he intended to marry, Jesus implied that he had determined not to become a father in the flesh for the sake of his hour and the Father's business [127:6.8].
41.034.h4: 3) Integration of Personality and Preparation for Mission
41.035.p: Through this period, Jesus succeeded in knitting his human and divine natures into a single, effective personality [127:6.9]. He learned to adjust ideals to reality, to wrest victory from the jaws of defeat, and to live a life in heaven while living on earth [127:6.12]. Now an adult, Jesus was ready to begin his supreme mission of revealing God to man and leading man to God [127:6.16].
42.title: Jesus’ Early and Later Manhood
42.001.h3: 1. Awareness as an Adult and Completion of Human Life
42.002.h4: 1) Realization of Dual Nature and 'Son of Man'
42.003.p: In his twenty-first year (A.D. 15), Jesus, having reached adulthood, entered upon the task of completing the experience of mastering the knowledge of the life of his lowest form of intelligent creatures with full self-consciousness [128:1.1]. Joshua ben Joseph knew full well that he was a mortal man, a fact evidenced by his selection of his first title, the "Son of Man" [128:1.2]. Regarding the attributes of his prehuman existence, he emptied himself, and prior to the beginning of his public work, his knowledge of men and events was self-limited [128:1.4]. Throughout all these years in the flesh, he was truly divine, yet he lived a human life and never once used supernatural power until the day of his baptism [128:1.9]~10.
42.004.h4: 2) Training as Head of Household and Study of Gentiles
42.005.p: In his twenty-second year (A.D. 16), Jesus formally installed his brother James as acting head of the household and began to train him by placing full financial responsibility upon him [128:2.4]. Jesus worked at the anvil in Sepphoris for six months, living with a Gentile and closely observing their habits of life and the Gentile mind [128:2.3], [128:2.5]. He returned to Nazareth because he disliked the low moral standards of Herod Antipas and was unwilling to work under his supervision; thereafter, he never again personally assumed the management of family affairs, permitting James to continue his oversight [128:2.6].
42.006.h4: 3) Visit to Jerusalem and Meeting Stephen
42.007.p: In his twenty-third year (A.D. 17), Jesus visited Jerusalem with Simon, becoming familiar with the whole of Palestine, and conversed about world affairs with a wealthy merchant from Damascus [128:3.2], [128:3.3]. Notably, Jesus spent four hours discussing the way of life and the true God with a young Hellenist named Stephen; Stephen was so impressed by this conversation that he later became the first martyr of the Christian faith [128:3.5]~6.
42.008.h3: 2. Worldly Temptations and Preparation for Separation
42.009.h4: 1) Rejection of the Damascus School Offer
42.010.p: Jesus received a proposal from a Damascus merchant who offered a vast sum of money to establish a school of religious philosophy and wanted Jesus to head it [128:4.1]. This was one of the greatest temptations Jesus faced in the course of his purely human activity, but he rejected it because he knew his mission was not to be supported by scholastic institutions or directed by a "board of men" [128:4.1]~2. Jesus sought to prevent the building of a brilliant career that might cause future generations to worship the teacher rather than obey his teachings, and he consistently tried to suppress such human achievements to avoid the temptation of building a religion [128:4.6].
42.012.p: In his twenty-fourth year (A.D. 18), Jesus was besought by prominent Jews from Alexandria to become a religious teacher in their synagogue, but he declined, saying, "My hour has not yet come" [128:5.2], [128:5.4]. They tried to persuade him by warning of the rebellion and destruction of Jerusalem, but Jesus refused even the purse they offered, sending them away by saying that the house of Joseph had never received charity and would not eat another's bread [128:5.3]~4.
42.013.h4: 3) Imprisonment of Judas and Family Weddings
42.014.p: In his twenty-fifth year (A.D. 19), Jesus visited Jerusalem with his brother Judas, who was arrested and imprisoned for expressing anger at a Roman guard [128:6.5]. Jesus appeared before the military magistrate, apologized on Judas's behalf, and secured his release through a judicious statement, though this incident prevented them from attending the temple services [128:6.6]~7. In November of his twenty-sixth year (A.D. 20), the double wedding of James to Esta and Miriam to Jacob took place, and Jesus entered into a secret compact with James, handing over full authority of the repair shop and formally abdicating as head of the family [128:7.10], [128:7.13].
42.015.h3: 3. Life in Capernaum and Experience as a Boatbuilder
42.016.h4: 1) Permanent Departure from Home and Boatbuilding
42.017.p: In January of his twenty-seventh year (A.D. 21), Jesus left his family and went to Capernaum to work at boatbuilding with Zebedee, a friend of his father [129:1.1], [129:1.2]. Jesus and Zebedee developed new techniques to build superior and safe boats, and Jesus became well known to the Galilean fishermen as the designer of the new boats [129:1.3].
